title: Lifting a split torus special kernel over a Noetherian local ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], put $k=R/\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-residue-field], and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For any finitely generated additive abelian group $M$, write $D_R(M)=\operatorname{Spec}R[M]$, where $R[M]$ has basis $e_m$ indexed by $m\in M$, multiplication $e_me_n=e_{m+n}$, comultiplication $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$, counit $e_m\mapsto1$, and inverse $e_m\mapsto e_{-m}$. An $S$-group scheme means an $S$-scheme with multiplication, identity section and inverse satisfying the group diagrams. Let $r\geq0$, let $P=D_R(\mathbf Z^r)=\mathbf G_{m,S}^r$ [def-sc-gm-ga], let $G$ be a separated $S$-group scheme of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $u:P\to G$ be an $S$-group homomorphism. Define $\ker(u_k)=P_k\times_{G_k,e_k}\operatorname{Spec}k$, with scheme-theoretic fibre products and base changes [def-pc-base-change]. There exists a subgroup $L\subseteq\mathbf Z^r$ such that the closed immersion $j:D_R(\mathbf Z^r/L)\hookrightarrow P$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], induced by $R[\mathbf Z^r]\twoheadrightarrow R[\mathbf Z^r/L]$, has closed fibre $j_k$ equal to $\ker(u_k)\hookrightarrow P_k$, and $u\circ j$ is the identity-valued homomorphism $D_R(\mathbf Z^r/L)\to G$.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Remark B.1.2 (printed p.280) and Corollary B.2.7 (p.287). Agent-formulated local consequence: split special-kernel subgroup, nilpotent rigidity, and coefficientwise Krull intersection; original not archived locally. No Stacks tag states the group-scheme lifting assertion.

proof.text: Put $v=e_G\circ p_P:P\to G$ and form the equalizer $K=P\times_{G\times_SG,(u,v),\Delta_G}G$. The definition of separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism] makes $\Delta_G$ a closed immersion; [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] therefore makes $K\to P$ a closed immersion. The fibre-product universal property identifies $K$ with $P\times_{G,u,e_G}S$: an equality $u(x)=e_G$ determines the common value in $G$ uniquely. The same universal property identifies its closed fibre with the kernel in the statement. On points over every $k$-algebra the kernel is closed under multiplication and inverse because $u_k$ preserves them. Restricting the multiplication and inverse morphisms through this fibre product therefore gives $K_k$ its group structure and makes $K_k\hookrightarrow P_k$ a group homomorphism. By [def-weil-closed-immersion] write $K_k=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and its inclusion as a surjection $q:k[\mathbf Z^r]\twoheadrightarrow B$. Here [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $P_k$ with the spectrum of $k[\mathbf Z^r]$: tensoring the displayed free monomial algebra with $k$ simply reduces its coefficients.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(c), printed p.234; the kernel and its closedness expanded using the separated diagonal

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf] to the affine $k$-group $K_k$. Pulling back the group-homomorphism diagrams for its inclusion shows that $b_a=q(e_a)$ is group-like, has counit $1$, and satisfies $b_ab_c=b_{a+c}$ and $b_a^{-1}=b_{-a}$. Let $L=\{a\in\mathbf Z^r:b_a=1\}$ and $M=\mathbf Z^r/L$. Since $a\mapsto b_a$ is a homomorphism into $B^\times$, $L$ is a subgroup and $b_a=b_c$ exactly when $a-c\in L$. Thus the distinct elements $b_{\bar a}$ indexed by $M$ span $B$ (apply $q$ to a finite monomial expansion). They are linearly independent by [lem-sfb-coalgebra-group-like-independent], whose base-field hypothesis holds for the residue field $k$; it does not require algebraic closedness or reducedness. Consequently $k[M]\to B$, $e_{\bar a}\mapsto b_a$, is a bijective algebra map. On the displayed basis it preserves coproduct, counit and antipode. Its composite with $k[\mathbf Z^r]\to k[M]$ is $q$. Hence, as a closed subscheme of $P_k$, $K_k$ is exactly $D_k(M)$ embedded by this quotient; the equality is scheme-theoretic, not just equality of geometric points. The images of the $r$ standard basis vectors generate $M$.

source.place: Theorems 12.8 and 12.9(c), printed pp.233-234; explicit image group and inclusion, using Proposition 4.23

proof.text: Set $H=D_R(M)$ and define $j:H\to P$ by $e_a\mapsto e_{\bar a}$. This algebra map is surjective since every basis element has a representative, so [def-weil-closed-immersion] makes $j$ a closed immersion. Its compatibility with coproduct, counit and antipode is checked on $e_a$: both coproduct composites send it to $e_{\bar a}\otimes e_{\bar a}$, both counits send it to $1$, and both antipode composites send it to $e_{-\bar a}$. Under the affine product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], these are precisely the three group-homomorphism diagrams. For any quotient $R\to A$, the coefficient map $R[M]\otimes_RA\to A[M]$ sends $e_m\otimes c$ to $ce_m$ and has inverse $ce_m\mapsto e_m\otimes c$, extended additively. Thus it identifies the base-changed group and inclusion with $D_A(M)\hookrightarrow D_A(\mathbf Z^r)$. For $A=k$, Step 2 gives $j_k=\ker(u_k)\hookrightarrow P_k$. In particular $f=u\circ j$ is identity-valued on the closed fibre.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(a),(c), pp.233-234; group-algebra construction over R and coefficient base change written explicitly

proof.text: For each $n\geq1$ put $A_n=R/\mathfrak m^n$ and $J_n=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^n\subseteq A_n$. Then $J_n^n=0$ and $A_n/J_n=k$. Apply [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-nilpotent-triviality] to $D_{A_n}(M)$, $G_{A_n}$ and $f_{A_n}$. The group $M$ is finitely generated by Step 2, the required base change of $H$ is the explicit one in Step 3, and the restriction of $f_{A_n}$ modulo $J_n$ is identity-valued by Step 3. Hence $f_{A_n}=e_{G_{A_n}}\circ p_{H_{A_n}}$ for every $n\geq1$. This application uses the arbitrary-target clause of the cited statement.

source.place: Corollary B.2.7, printed p.287, applied over R/m^n

proof.text: Form the equalizer $E$ of $f:H\to G$ and $e_G\circ p_H$. As in Step 1, it is the pullback of the closed diagonal of $G$, so [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] and [def-weil-closed-immersion] give $E=\operatorname{Spec}(R[M]/I)$ for an ideal $I\subseteq R[M]$. For each $n$, Step 4 says that $H_{A_n}\to H$ factors through $E$. On rings this means $I$ maps to zero in $A_n[M]$; equivalently every coefficient of every $x\in I$ lies in $\mathfrak m^n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] with ring $R$, ideal $\mathfrak m$ and finite module $R$: $R$ is Noetherian, $R$ is generated by $1$ as an $R$-module, and the unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ is the Jacobson radical. It gives $\bigcap_n\mathfrak m^n=0$. Write $x\in I$ as a finite sum $\sum_m c_me_m$. Each $c_m$ is in that intersection, hence zero, so $I=0$. Therefore $E=H$ and $f=e_G\circ p_H$. This proves the required identity-valued assertion together with the special-fibre equality already proved in Step 3; Krull intersection was applied only to the finite module $R$, not to the generally infinite free module $R[M]$.

source.place: Tag 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module), part (2), applied coefficientwise; equalizer as in Step 1

Source: Conrad, Reductive group schemes. I fetched the author's PDF read-only because it is not in literature/. Corollary B.2.7 (printed p.287) says verbatim that if J^{n+1}=0, a homomorphism H→G from a multiplicative-type H to an ARBITRARY S-group scheme G that is trivial over S0 is trivial. The new node lem-sfb-diagonalizable-nilpotent-triviality is exactly the split case D_A(M), M finitely generated, J^N=0, and its hypotheses match one for one. I also checked it independently: the difference derivation is primitive in J⊗A[M], so it is zero. Remark B.1.2 (p.280) supports the item's subgroup description. Step 1: the kernel is the pullback of the closed diagonal (separatedness), so K_k is affine and closed in P_k. Step 2: the coordinate-ring Hopf node and the group-like independence node both work over an arbitrary field, giving k[M]≅B compatibly with q. It correctly avoids the algebraically-closed-field subgroup node. Step 3 is an elementary base change. Step 4 applies the new node over A_n=R/m^n with J_n=m/m^n, J_n^n=0. Step 5 forces every coefficient of I into m^n, and Krull on the finite module R gives I=0. Edge cases checked: r=0, L=0, L=Z^r, R a field, R=k[ε], μ_p in characteristic p; for the new node M=0, J=0 and J=A. lean.statement: theorem splitLocalSpecialKernelLifting (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (r : ℕ) (G : Over (Spec (.of R))) [GrpObj G] [IsSeparated G.hom] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation G.hom] [QuasiCompact G.hom] [QuasiSeparated G.hom] (f : (ringDiagonalizableGroup R (Fin r → ULift.{u} ℤ)).X ⟶ G) [IsMonHom f] : ∃ L : AddSubgroup (Fin r → ULift.{u} ℤ), IsClosedImmersion (ringDiagonalizableGroupMap R (QuotientAddGroup.mk' L)).hom.hom.left ∧ IsPullback (((Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IsLocalRing.residue R)))).map (ringDiagonalizableGroupMap R (QuotientAddGroup.mk' L)).hom.hom).left) (((Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IsLocalRing.residue R)))).map (toUnit (ringDiagonalizableGroup R ((Fin r → ULift.{u} ℤ) ⧸ L)).X)).left) (((Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IsLocalRing.residue R)))).map f).left) (((Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IsLocalRing.residue R)))).map η[G]).left) ∧ (ringDiagonalizableGroupMap R (QuotientAddGroup.mk' L)).hom.hom ≫ f = toUnit (ringDiagonalizableGroup R ((Fin r → ULift.{u} ℤ) ⧸ L)).X ≫ η[G]
